You are a scientist running experiments on an unknown system.

A 6x6 board (rows and columns numbered 0-5) hides three ships: lengths 4, 3 and 2, each horizontal or vertical, never overlapping. They were placed by exactly ONE of the placement rules below. Each experiment is one action, written as a design: [0, row, col] fires at one cell (cost 1) and reports 1 (hit) or 0 (miss), but the report is wrong with probability 0.1; [1, 0, i] scans row i and [1, 1, i] scans column i (cost 2) and report the number of ship cells in that whole row or column, off by -1 / +1 with probability 0.15 / 0.15 each, then clipped to 0-6. Actions never change the board; repeating one draws fresh noise.

Exact generative model: (1) a rule is drawn uniformly at random from the list (each 1/6); (2) the layout is drawn uniformly from ALL layouts that satisfy that rule (a layout can satisfy several rules; 'any' is satisfied by every layout); (3) each action's noise is independent.
Rules:
1. any (53624 layouts): No constraint: any layout in which the three ships do not overlap.
2. no_touch (11520 layouts): No two ships touch, not even diagonally: no cell of one ship is among the 8 neighbours of a cell of another ship.
3. parallel (15960 layouts): All three ships have the same orientation (all horizontal or all vertical).
4. border (16864 layouts): Every ship has at least one cell on the outer edge of the board (row 0 or 5, or column 0 or 5).
5. center_clear (19208 layouts): No ship covers any of the four centre cells (rows 2-3, columns 2-3).
6. clustered (14848 layouts): Every ship touches at least one other ship (8-neighbourhood: sharing an edge or a corner counts).
Prior probability that each cell is covered by a ship (row 0 first):
0.165 0.233 0.280 0.280 0.233 0.165
0.233 0.255 0.272 0.272 0.255 0.233
0.280 0.272 0.260 0.260 0.272 0.280
0.280 0.272 0.260 0.260 0.272 0.280
0.233 0.255 0.272 0.272 0.255 0.233
0.165 0.233 0.280 0.280 0.233 0.165

Your budget is 20: every action spends its cost, and an action you cannot afford is rejected. Choose each one to learn as much as possible; you will then be asked for the probability of each rule and, for every cell, the probability that a ship covers it. Your answer is scored by the log of the probability it assigns to the truth relative to the prior, so be calibrated: confident where the evidence supports it, uncertain where it does not.

To run an experiment, reply with your reasoning followed by exactly one tag, e.g. <observe>[0, 2, 3]</observe>. To stop experimenting early, reply <done/>.
In the final phase you must answer with a JSON object {"rules": {name: probability, ...}, "occupancy": 6 rows of 6 probabilities}, and nothing after it.
